tasks.spec:
Create a file named greet.py in the current working directory.

It must define a function greet(name) that returns the string 'Hello, <name>!' where <name> is the argument.

It must also run as a script: when executed directly with `python3 greet.py`, it prints exactly `Hello, Ringer!` and nothing else.

Use only the Python standard library. Do not create any other files. Do not print anything on import.
tasks.check: out=$(python3 greet.py 2>&1); rc=$?; if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then echo "FAIL: 'python3 greet.py' exited $rc. Output was:"; echo "$out"; exit 1; fi; if [ "$out" != "Hello, Ringer!" ]; then echo "FAIL: expected stdout 'Hello, Ringer!' but got '$out'"; exit 1; fi; python3 -c "import greet; r = greet.greet('World'); assert r == 'Hello, World!', 'FAIL: greet(\"World\") returned %r, expected \"Hello, World!\"' % r; print('OK: script output and greet() both correct')" || exit 1
tasks.verified: greet.py runs as a script printing exactly 'Hello, Ringer!' and its greet() function returns the right string for a different name too.
